result.summary: This PR fixes stale -proxy help text and Tor documentation that still referenced the removed 'tor' network name (removed in #34031), causing startup failures for users following the examples. It refactors -proxy's network-name parsing in init.cpp to reuse the shared network parser already used by -onlynet and getnodeaddresses, making behavior consistent (case-insensitive matching, unsupported names echoed verbatim). Tests were added/expanded in feature_proxy.py and rpc_net.py to characterize the previous behavior and cover the fix, including a pre-existing gap around clearing the IPv4 proxy also clearing the name proxy.
result.problem: Users following the shipped -proxy help text or doc/tor.md examples (e.g. -proxy=addr:port=tor) hit a startup error because 'tor' was removed as a valid network name in #34031, and the -proxy code duplicated its own network-name mapping instead of using the shared parser used elsewhere.

result.card: This PR fixes a startup failure that hits users who follow Bitcoin Core's own -proxy help text or doc/tor.md examples, which still reference the 'tor' network name removed in #34031. It refactors -proxy's ad hoc network-name mapping in init.cpp to reuse the shared parser already used by -onlynet and getnodeaddresses, adding tests for case-insensitivity, rejection of the removed 'tor' name, and a pre-existing gap around clearing the IPv4 proxy. Reviewer jeanpablojp gave a Concept ACK after building and running the affected functional tests, and every follow-up nit (doc wording, a widened test comment, added coverage) was incorporated by the author in a force push, leaving no open objections. The PR is small, labeled P2P, and touches doc/tor.md, src/init.cpp, and two functional test files; it has no stacking or blocking dependencies.
